title: Lie and Hall algebra actions with controlled decategorification

items.title: Spin weight spaces and rank-one Hall realization
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited through the cited Hall supplier. Let
$V=\mathbb C^2$ with ordered orthonormal basis $|\uparrow\rangle,|\downarrow\rangle$.
On $V$ define
$$ E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad H=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}. $$
They satisfy $[H,E]=2E$, $[H,F]=-2F$, and $[E,F]=H$, and therefore define
the standard two-dimensional representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$.
Write $S^+=E$, $S^-=F$, and $S^z=H/2$.

For each integer $N\geq1$, the spin space is
$\mathcal H_N=V^{\otimes N}$ with its tensor-product inner product. If $A$ is
an endomorphism of $V$, let $A_j$ act as $A$ on factor $j$ and as the identity
on the other factors. Define the diagonal generators
$$ S_N^+=\sum_{j=1}^N E_j,\qquad S_N^-=\sum_{j=1}^N F_j,\qquad S_N^z=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^N H_j. $$
For $m\in\{-N/2,-N/2+1,\ldots,N/2\}$, its weight space is
$\mathcal H_{N,m}=\ker(S_N^z-mI)$. These are dimensionless matrices in the
algebraic spin convention.

For each integer $r\geq0$, define $V(r)$ to be the vector space
$\mathbb C[x,y]_r$ of homogeneous polynomials of degree $r$, with
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action
$$ E=x\partial_y,\qquad F=y\partial_x,\qquad H=x\partial_x-y\partial_y. $$
The ordered monomials $x^{r-k}y^k$ for $0\leq k\leq r$ form its basis.
Under $x\mapsto|\uparrow\rangle$ and $y\mapsto|\downarrow\rangle$,
$V(1)$ is the representation on $V$ above. A tensor power $V(1)^{\otimes N}$
uses the diagonal action defined by the sums $S_N^+,S_N^-,2S_N^z$.

Let $q_H>1$ be a prime power, fix a finite field $\mathbb F_{q_H}$, and put
$\nu=\sqrt{q_H}>1$ and $K=\mathbb Q(\nu)$. The representation category
$\mathcal A=\mathrm{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}}_{\mathbb F_{q_H}}$ of the one-vertex,
no-arrow quiver has one simple isomorphism class, represented by
$S=\mathbb F_{q_H}$. For objects $M,N$, write
$\chi_0(M,N)=\dim_{\mathbb F_{q_H}}\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)-
\dim_{\mathbb F_{q_H}}\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N)$. In the Hall convention of
[[def-euler-twisted-hall-algebra]], the Hall space is
$H_{\mathcal A,\nu}=\bigoplus_{[M]}K[M]$, with basis $[M]$ indexed by
isomorphism classes and product
$$[M]\star[N]=\nu^{\chi_0(M,N)}\sum_{[L]}g^L_{M,N}[L],$$
where $g^L_{M,N}$ counts subspaces $N'\subseteq L$ with $N'\cong N$ and
$L/N'\cong M$, or equivalently short exact sequences
$0\to N\to L\to M\to0$. Thus the twist is part of the multiplication.
For $M\cong\mathbb F_{q_H}^{m}$ and $N\cong\mathbb F_{q_H}^{n}$,
$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)=mn$ and every short exact sequence splits, so
$\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N)=0$ and $\chi_0(M,N)=mn$.

By [[def-extended-hall-algebra-and-composition-subalgebra]], the composition
subalgebra is the subalgebra of this Hall algebra generated by the classes of
simple objects; its torus extension is the distinct extended composition
subalgebra. Denote the former by $\mathcal C$ here, so
$\mathcal C=K\langle[S]\rangle\subseteq H_{\mathcal A,\nu}$. The rank-one
positive quantum half is $U_\nu^+(\mathfrak{sl}_2)=K[E]$, the polynomial
algebra on one generator. The Ringel map $E\mapsto[S]$ embeds this positive
half with image $\mathcal C$; since the one-vertex graph is finite Dynkin type
$A_1$, the finite-Dynkin criterion identifies $\mathcal C$ with the full Hall
algebra in this case. The simple object is unique up to isomorphism, not as a
chosen representative. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the cited
Ringel supplier.

references.locator: Lecture 3, Theorem 3.16 and proof, PDF pp. 39–40: the Ringel–Green embedding and the finite-type criterion.

references.title: Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures 1993

items.title: Exchange preserves total Lie spin
items.statement:
Let $N\geq2$, let $\mathcal H_N=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$, and let the
diagonal spin generators $S_N^+,S_N^-,S_N^z$ be the sums of the one-site
matrices $E,F,H/2$ defined in the spin convention. For any distinct sites
$i,j$, let $P_{ij}$ exchange tensor factors $i$ and $j$. Then
$$ [P_{ij},S_N^+]=[P_{ij},S_N^-]=[P_{ij},S_N^z]=0. $$

For $N\geq3$, take an auxiliary copy $V_a=\mathbb C^2$ and define
$P_{aj}$ as the flip of $V_a$ and site $j$. Fix the ordered orthonormal basis
of $V_a$ inherited from $V$. For $X\in\operatorname{End}(V_a\otimes\mathcal H_N)$,
write $X=\sum_{r,s=1}^2E_{rs}\otimes X_{rs}$ in this basis, where $E_{rs}$
are its matrix units and $X_{rs}\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H_N)$, and
define the partial trace by $\operatorname{tr}_aX:=X_{11}+X_{22}$. With
$$ R_{aj}(u)=uI+iP_{aj},\qquad T_a(u)=R_{aN}(u)\cdots R_{a1}(u),\qquad t(u)=\operatorname{tr}_a T_a(u)\quad(u\in\mathbb C), $$
where products act rightmost first, every transfer matrix preserves the
diagonal spin action:
$$ [t(u),S_N^+]=[t(u),S_N^-]=[t(u),S_N^z]=0. $$
Use the periodic convention $P_{N,N+1}=P_{N,1}$. For real $J,c$, the
periodic XXX matrix
$$ H_N=J\sum_{j=1}^N P_{j,j+1}+cI $$
is Hermitian and commutes with all three generators. When $H_N$ is interpreted as a
physical energy, $J$ and $c$ have joule units; $u$ is dimensionless.

For $m\in\{-N/2,-N/2+1,\ldots,N/2\}$, set
$\mathcal H_{N,m}=\ker(S_N^z-mI)$. For real $\beta$, define the finite
matrix exponential by $\exp(A)=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}A^r/r!$, converging in
operator norm, and let $\operatorname{Tr}_W(B)$ denote the trace of a
finite-dimensional endomorphism $B:W\to W$, namely the matrix trace in any
basis (independent of that basis). Put
$Z_N(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_N}(\exp(-\beta H_N))$. Then
$$ Z_N(\beta)=\sum_m \operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_{N,m}} \left(\exp(-\beta H_N)\big|_{\mathcal H_{N,m}}\right). $$
In a physical Gibbs interpretation, $\beta$ has inverse-joule units.

items.title: KLR grading gives integral multiplicity bookkeeping
items.statement:
Let $D$ be a KLR datum on a symmetrizable Cartan datum with no imaginary
simple roots, over a field $k$, in the conventions of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. Let $R_D$
be the resulting graded KLR algebra, and let $K_0(R_D)$ be the Grothendieck
group of its graded projectives. Put
$\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[q_{\mathrm{gr}},q_{\mathrm{gr}}^{-1}]$, where
$q_{\mathrm{gr}}$ is the Laurent grading variable denoted by $q$ in the
divided-power integral form, and let $\mathcal A f_D$ be the integral
negative quantum half. The canonical map
$\gamma_D:\mathcal A f_D\to K_0(R_D)$ is an isomorphism of
$\mathcal A$-algebras and graded twisted bialgebras; $q_{\mathrm{gr}}$ records
the grading shift. Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited through this supplier.

For each integer $n\geq1$, the irreducible highest-weight-$n$ module $V(n)$
defined by homogeneous polynomials of degree $n$ has $H$-weights
$n,n-2,\ldots,-n$, each with multiplicity one. The diagonal
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module
$V(1)^{\otimes n}$ has $H$-weight $n-2k$ with multiplicity
$\binom nk$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Here $H=2S^z$.

For real $h$ and $\beta$, define the zero-exchange finite matrix
$H_n^{(0)}=-hS_n^z$ on $V(1)^{\otimes n}$. Use
$\exp(A)=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}A^r/r!$ for the finite-dimensional matrix
exponential, convergent in operator norm, and let $\operatorname{Tr}$ denote
the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional endomorphism. Define its
partition trace by
$Z_n(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{V(1)^{\otimes n}}\exp(-\beta H_n^{(0)})$.
Then
$$ Z_n(\beta)=\bigl(2\cosh(\beta h/2)\bigr)^n, \qquad \cosh x:=\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}2. $$
For a Gibbs interpretation, $h$ is an energy coefficient, $S_n^z$ is
dimensionless, and $\beta$ has inverse-energy units. The KLR isomorphism
supplies the negative-half categorification stated above; it supplies no
identification with either finite-dimensional spin module, no
tensor-product categorical realization, and no spin-chain energy spectrum.

title: Lie and Hall algebra actions with controlled decategorification — Examples

items.title: Equal representation structure need not fix energy
items.statement:
Fix $W=V(1)\otimes V(1)$ with its tensor-product inner product and its diagonal
representation $\rho:\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(W)$
from the spin convention, together with the rank-one Hall data at $q_H=2$ and
the type-$A_1$ KLR negative-half Grothendieck isomorphism over $\mathbb Q$.
Let
$$\mathscr H_\rho=\{A\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(W):A=A^*,\ [A,\rho(X)]=0\text{ for every }X\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\},$$
where $A^*$ is the adjoint for the stated inner product. For an endomorphism
$D$ of $W$, set $\exp(D)=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}D^r/r!$, convergent in operator
norm, and let $\operatorname{Tr}_W$ denote the basis-independent trace on
endomorphisms of $W$. For
$C\in\mathscr H_\rho$ and $\beta\geq0$, define its partition trace by
$$Z_C(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_W(\exp(-\beta C)).$$
The claim that the fixed algebraic data
uniquely determine the spectrum and partition trace of every member of
$\mathscr H_\rho$ means that any $A,B\in\mathscr H_\rho$ have the same
eigenvalues counted with algebraic multiplicity and satisfy
$$Z_A(\beta)=Z_B(\beta)\quad\text{for every }\beta\geq0.$$
This uniqueness claim is false. If the endomorphisms are interpreted as
energies, $\beta$ has inverse-energy units.
